crowdsec.activity.empty: No attacks were recorded in this time window.
crowdsec.activity.summary: {total, plural, one {# attack} other {# attacks}} in the selected {hours, plural, one {hour} other {# hours}}. The busiest interval contains {peak}.
crowdsec.anubis-report.coverage-help: Saved configuration only; this does not prove a successful challenge. Custom locations inherit the host when their provider is unset or None. Advanced nginx overrides are not evaluated. Metrics cannot identify individual hosts in this auth-request deployment.
crowdsec.anubis-report.custom: Custom upstream configured; shared metrics may not apply
crowdsec.anubis-report.empty: No retained observations in this window. History starts after the first collector baseline.
crowdsec.anubis-report.gap: A source reset, collection gap, or pending batch was detected. This is incomplete history.
crowdsec.anubis-report.history-help: Address timestamps show when the collector noticed an entry, not its original hit time. Ban timestamps identify command attempts, not blocked traffic. Latest 20,000 records are retained for up to seven days. Anubis batches and resets its source log, so this history can be incomplete.
crowdsec.anubis-report.metrics-help: Challenges issued, successful validations, and failed validation attempts are separate counters for the installer-managed Anubis instance. They are not unique visitors or a pass rate.
crowdsec.anubis-report.partial: Partial coverage. Missing metrics and collection gaps are not counted as zero. Five-minute intervals are retained for seven days.
crowdsec.anubis-report.refresh-failed: Refresh failed. Displayed reporting is stale.
crowdsec.anubis-report.title: Anubis outcomes
crowdsec.anubis-unreachable: Anubis is not reachable from NPMplus.
crowdsec.anubis.active: {count, plural, one {# active honeypot ban} other {# active honeypot bans}}
crowdsec.anubis.active-at-least: At least {count, plural, one {# active honeypot decision} other {# active honeypot decisions}}
crowdsec.anubis.bridge-counts: Last run: {applied} ban commands accepted, {failed} failed; {pending} bytes pending. These are not traffic-block counts.
crowdsec.anubis.bridge-failed: Last run failed; pending entries need retry
crowdsec.anubis.bridge-idle: Last run had no new bytes
crowdsec.anubis.bridge-unavailable: Not observed; requires updated host tooling
crowdsec.anubis.container-down: Anubis is down or not wired up
crowdsec.anubis.decisions-unavailable: Honeypot-ban counts are temporarily unavailable from CrowdSec. Anubis health is shown separately.
crowdsec.anubis.empty: No honeypot bans are active right now
crowdsec.anubis.honeypot-help: Status checks Anubis reachability and whether its trap log is readable. Active bans created by the five-minute CrowdSec bridge are reported separately.
crowdsec.anubis.honeypot-waiting: Honeypot ready; waiting for its first catch
crowdsec.anubis.items-limited: Showing {count} honeypot decisions. Open Active bans to browse the local list.
crowdsec.anubis.log-truncated: Counts cover complete valid addresses in the last 256 KiB of the log only.
crowdsec.anubis.reporting-scope: Service reachability and a readable log do not prove that challenges or bans work. Retained address entries have no event timestamps. Log modification time is not a per-IP hit time.
crowdsec.anubis.title: Anubis
crowdsec.anubis.unconfigured: Anubis is not configured for this stack (no AUTH_REQUEST_ANUBIS_UPSTREAM)
crowdsec.appsec.blocked-help: Requests blocked by AppSec since CrowdSec started; repeated requests from one IP count separately
crowdsec.appsec.compatibility-help: The default high-confidence rules are designed to avoid false positives. If a legitimate upload, API, or webhook is blocked, exempt only that proxy host or custom location instead of disabling CrowdSec globally.
crowdsec.appsec.decisions-help: A WAF block rejects a request without necessarily creating an IP ban. Active local decisions can be zero while this counter is above zero.
crowdsec.appsec.description: CrowdSec AppSec inspects web requests before they reach your proxied applications and blocks high-confidence exploit attempts.
crowdsec.appsec.enable-help: AppSec is not configured. Enable it through the safe installer update:
crowdsec.appsec.failure-deny: Block requests if AppSec cannot answer
crowdsec.appsec.failure-passthrough: Keep sites available if AppSec cannot answer
crowdsec.appsec.host-toggle-help: Use the “CrowdSec AppSec protection” switch in a proxy host or custom location. Turning it off there disables only WAF inspection; normal CrowdSec bans remain enforced.
crowdsec.appsec.passed-help: Inspected requests minus AppSec blocks; other protection layers may still reject them
crowdsec.appsec.rules-default: Installer default: virtual patches and generic rules. The loaded policy is not reported here.
crowdsec.appsec.title: Web application firewall
crowdsec.appsec.top-rules-help: Rule triggers since CrowdSec started. One request may trigger multiple rules, including out-of-band rules; these are not individual blocked requests.
crowdsec.appsec.traffic-summary: AppSec inspected {requests} requests: {passed} passed and {blocked} were blocked.
crowdsec.appsec.unreadable-allow: Allow requests whose body cannot be inspected
crowdsec.appsec.unreadable-drop: Block requests whose body cannot be inspected
crowdsec.attack-map.motion-note: Meteors fly from observed origins toward your instance; they do not represent network routes.
crowdsec.attack-map.summary: {count, plural, one {# attack} other {# attacks}} plotted across {countries, plural, one {# country} other {# countries}}.
crowdsec.attack-map.top-origins: Top {count} origin groups are plotted; {rest, plural, one {# more group} other {# more groups}} {rest, plural, one {is} other {are}} not shown.
crowdsec.attack-mix.filter: Show only {scenario} in the activity tab
crowdsec.attack-mix.summary: {total, plural, one {# attack} other {# attacks}} in the selected {hours, plural, one {hour} other {# hours}}, grouped by attack type.
crowdsec.audit-warning: The ban was removed, but final audit status could not be saved. The original request remains in the audit log.
crowdsec.bad-key: CrowdSec rejected the bouncer key — it was deleted or the key file is stale. Re-register it with: docker exec crowdsec cscli bouncers add npmplus-ui -o raw | sudo tee /opt/npmplus/crowdsec/lapi-ui.key >/dev/null
crowdsec.bad-machine-key: CrowdSec rejected the machine login (usually after an unclean shutdown rolled its database back). Heal it with: sudo /usr/local/bin/npmplus-crowdsec-heal - or re-register manually: docker exec crowdsec cscli machines add npmplus-ui -a -f - --force 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^password: //p' | sudo tee /opt/npmplus/crowdsec/lapi-ui-machine.key >/dev/null
crowdsec.ban-target.help: A single IP (1.2.3.4) or a range (1.2.3.0/24)
crowdsec.capi-no-local-alerts: This ban comes from the CrowdSec community blocklist: the attack was reported by other community members, not observed on this server, so no local attack details exist.
crowdsec.empty-local: No local bans are active right now.
crowdsec.evidence.detected: Detection evidence only. A rule match does not prove a successful exploit, an active IP ban, or a request blocked at the client.
crowdsec.evidence.honeypot: The honeypot log records an address caught by the trap. Bridge events describe attempts to submit a ban to CrowdSec; they are not additional attacks.
crowdsec.evidence.honeypot-limits: This record has no request path, User-Agent, payload, or tool fingerprint. The time is when the collector observed the record. Active-ban status is the current decision state, not proof that this request was blocked.
crowdsec.evidence.no-events: No request evidence was supplied. Target, client tool, and per-request outcome are unknown.
crowdsec.evidence.related-error: Related alerts are unavailable. This does not mean no attack was detected.
crowdsec.evidence.related-help: Bounded recent alerts for the same IP. They may describe separate activity and are not proof of the tool or request that triggered this honeypot record. Compare detection times and rule names.
crowdsec.evidence.sample: Showing {shown} retained event records; the detector reports {count} events. Details are capped at 10 records and may be incomplete.
crowdsec.evidence.simulated: Simulation: this alert does not establish an enforced ban.
crowdsec.evidence.tool-help: This hint comes only from the recorded User-Agent and can be spoofed. An HTTP client is not proof of an attack tool or an attacker?s identity.
crowdsec.evidence.type-brute: Suggested attack type: repeated authentication attempts / brute force.
crowdsec.evidence.type-cve: Suggested attack type: probe for a named CVE. A match does not establish that the target is vulnerable.
crowdsec.evidence.type-execution: Suggested attack type: command or code execution attempt.
crowdsec.evidence.type-exposure: Suggested attack type: access to a sensitive configuration file.
crowdsec.evidence.type-file: Suggested attack type: path traversal or file inclusion attempt.
crowdsec.evidence.type-flood: Suggested attack type: excessive request rate / flooding.
crowdsec.evidence.type-manual: Decision type: manually supplied reason; no attack classification is established.
crowdsec.evidence.type-probing: Suggested attack type: endpoint scanning or enumeration.
crowdsec.evidence.type-sql: Suggested attack type: SQL injection attempt.
crowdsec.evidence.type-unknown: Attack type is not classified from this identifier. Use the recorded rule and event evidence.
crowdsec.evidence.type-xss: Suggested attack type: cross-site scripting attempt.
crowdsec.evidence.unknown-tool: Unknown ? no recognized tool claim in the recorded User-Agent.
crowdsec.evidence.waf-aggregate: These are aggregate rule matches, not individual attacker records. One request can match several rules. Inspect Attack activity for retained alerts; tool identity and per-IP enforcement cannot be derived from these counters.
crowdsec.history.batch-empty: No matching attacks in this batch. Use Next if older batches are available.
crowdsec.history.batch-matches: {count, plural, one {# match in this batch} other {# matches in this batch}}
crowdsec.history.cursor-invalid: This exploration expired or changed. Restart exploration to continue.
crowdsec.history.empty: No local attacks were recorded in this time window.
crowdsec.history.sampled: This view reached its safe response limit. Refine the filters or use a shorter time window to see more precise results.
crowdsec.history.scan-help: Browse older alerts in bounded batches, ordered by recording time. Filters apply to each batch: an empty batch can still have older matches. This does not expand the sampled overview or provide an exhaustive total.
crowdsec.history.scan-limit: Exploration stopped at a safety limit or a dense timestamp boundary. Older alerts may remain; narrow the window or investigate directly in CrowdSec.
crowdsec.history.search: Search, or use ip:, scenario:, country:, target:, asn:, machine:
crowdsec.history.title: Alert history
crowdsec.insights.alerts: {count, plural, one {# alert} other {# alerts}} in the last 24h
crowdsec.insights.sampled: Only a bounded sample of this window is available. Counts are lower bounds; charts and rankings describe that sample.
crowdsec.invalid-ban-input: Manual ban rejected: invalid target, duration, or reason.
crowdsec.invalid-response: CrowdSec returned an invalid or oversized response.
crowdsec.kpi.attacks-hint: Detection alerts in the last {hours, plural, one {hour} other {# hours}}; excludes simulations and dashboard manual bans
crowdsec.kpi.bouncer-hits: {count, plural, one {# non-empty decision reply} other {# non-empty decision replies}} since CrowdSec started. Includes dashboard reads; this does not verify blocked traffic or current enforcement.
crowdsec.kpi.bouncer-idle: No bouncer API requests recorded. Current enforcement cannot be determined from this counter.
crowdsec.kpi.bouncer-pulls: {count, plural, one {# bouncer API request} other {# bouncer API requests}} since CrowdSec started. This is not a count of blocked requests.
crowdsec.kpi.community-help: Community and blocklist decision totals from CrowdSec metrics. These feeds are enforced by configured remediation components and have no individual unban controls here. This count alone does not verify current enforcement.
crowdsec.kpi.community-hint: Current community and blocklist decision records
crowdsec.kpi.community-metrics-degraded: Community totals are unavailable from the current metrics
crowdsec.kpi.local-help: Current local ban and CAPTCHA decisions, excluding simulations. Honeypot decisions are counted separately. A + marks a lower bound from a capped sample; these are decision records, not unique IP addresses or blocked requests. WAF request blocks do not necessarily create an ongoing decision. Expired or removed decisions are no longer counted here.
crowdsec.kpi.local-hint: Ban/CAPTCHA decisions active now, excluding honeypots and simulations
crowdsec.lapi-error: CrowdSec Local API could not complete the request.
crowdsec.local-only-help: Only decisions created by this instance are listed. Community protection remains active in the background.
crowdsec.location-empty: No geolocation was recorded for alerts in this window.
crowdsec.matches-at-least: At least {count, plural, one {# match} other {# matches}}
crowdsec.metrics-unavailable: CrowdSec metrics are unavailable. Alert history and bans still work normally.
crowdsec.metrics-unconfigured: CrowdSec metrics are not configured for this stack.
crowdsec.metrics.since-restart: Request and whitelist counters are cumulative since CrowdSec started. Latencies and parser success summarize that period; the activity time selector does not change them.
crowdsec.metrics.title: Engine metrics since restart
crowdsec.metrics.whitelist-hits-help: Successful whitelist-node matches since CrowdSec started; one event can match more than one node
crowdsec.no-alerts: No alert context kept for this ban (alerts are pruned after their retention)
crowdsec.not-wired: CrowdSec monitoring is not wired up: the backend needs the bouncer key file /data/crowdsec/lapi-ui.key, created by setup-npmplus.sh when crowdsec is enabled
crowdsec.not-wired-machine: CrowdSec unban is not wired up: the backend needs the machine key file /data/crowdsec/lapi-ui-machine.key, created by setup-npmplus.sh when crowdsec is enabled
crowdsec.notification.bans: CrowdSec is enforcing {count, plural, one {# active ban} other {# active bans}}.
crowdsec.notification.spike: CrowdSec detected an unusual spike in attacks.
crowdsec.notification.unavailable: The CrowdSec Local API is unavailable.
crowdsec.notifications.blocked-help: Browser notifications are blocked. Allow notifications for this site in your browser settings, then try again.
crowdsec.page-too-deep: That page is outside the safe live-query limit. Refine the filters or use a shorter window.
crowdsec.partial-refresh: The latest refresh failed for part of the dashboard. Showing the last successful results.
crowdsec.partial-unavailable: Some security details are temporarily unavailable. CrowdSec enforcement continues independently.
crowdsec.simulated-help: Simulated decisions are dry runs from a test scenario: they never block traffic.
crowdsec.spike-warning: Attack activity is unusually high in the latest time bucket.
crowdsec.stale: The latest refresh failed. Showing the last successful result.
crowdsec.tabs.label: Security dashboard sections
crowdsec.telemetry.host-limit: Showing up to 200 hosts; totals include other recorded hosts.
crowdsec.telemetry.layers-help: Counts record invoked nginx remediation actions and IPv4 INPUT/FORWARD dropped packets. These are different units and must not be added together. Recent observations are timestamped evidence, not a guarantee of continuous protection or completed response delivery.
crowdsec.telemetry.partial: Partial history: collection has just started, a source restarted, a limit was reached, or observations are missing. Counts cover recorded intervals only; missing history is not zero traffic.
crowdsec.telemetry.rules-present: Service active; INPUT and FORWARD drop rules present
crowdsec.telemetry.unavailable: Telemetry unavailable. Update the image and installer to enable collection.
crowdsec.telemetry.waf-help: Confirmed responses include AppSec allow and deny verdicts. Policy denials include configured fail-closed and unreadable-body handling. Challenge pages are counted separately under System. This history covers managed proxy hosts and retains seven days.
crowdsec.telemetry.window: {start} to {end}. Completed five-minute intervals; collected every minute. Window boundaries are approximate to one collection interval.
crowdsec.title: CrowdSec Bans
crowdsec.truncated-bans: The live list is capped at {limit} entries; more bans may exist than shown.
crowdsec.unavailable: CrowdSec Local API is unavailable or timed out.
crowdsec.unban-content: CrowdSec will delete decision #{id}. The target can be banned again if it keeps offending.
